data.name: Bikr
data.gender_notes: Bikr is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Arabic root 'b-k-r', meaning 'to be alive, to be awake, or to be alert'. This name is mentioned in the Quran and is associated with Prophet Ibrahim's servant, al-Khidr. It signifies a person who is full of energy, life, and consciousness, always alert and responsive to the will of God. The name Bikr carries the meaning “Vigor, Energy” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Bikr usually hope their child will grow to embody vigor, energy and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name that embodies spiritual awakening and alertness to the presence of God.
data.etymology: Bikr belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Vigor, Energy.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Bikr total 4, giving a life-path number of 4. Number 4 is linked with Rahu and with the qualities of stability, discipline and hard work.

historical_references.context: Bikr ibn Wa'il (Abu Jahl), a prominent Meccan leader, was the first to openly challenge the growing Muslim community by organizing a military expedition against them during the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah. Bikr's army was defeated, and he was killed in the battle.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Ibn Hisham, Al-Sirah Al-Nabawiyyah, Volume III, p. 537. The name Bikr carried significant weight in that era.
historical_references.context: Bikr ibn Hittab (As-Siddiq Ibn Al-Aas), the governor of Medina during the Prophet Muhammad's absence, declared his disbelief and led a rebellion against the Muslim community. He was defeated and killed in the Battle of the Trench, which was a significant turning point in the early Islamic history.
